Below is the consolidated 12-week, cycle-aware program for your 28‑year‑old recreational lifter. It integrates strength (3x/week), intensified Phase 2 strength, aerobic base cardio (3x/week), one weekly HIIT metabolic session, one weekly power/plyometric session, nutrition for cycle‑related fatigue/cramping, and guidance for cycle-aware 1RM testing at the end of the block. Flow days (menstrual days 1–3) are treated as restrictive: no high‑intensity, no heavy Valsalva, no jumping. If her cycle dates shift, apply the same flow-day rules to whichever days are menstrual days.

Dates and cycle mapping (based on last period 2026-05-01, 28‑day cycle)
- Program start: 2026-06-01 (Mon)
- Expected flow windows during program:
  - Jun 26–28 (Week 4)
  - Jul 24–26 (Week 8)
  - Aug 21–23 (Week 12)
- If her actual period timing differs, move the “flow‑day” modifications to the relevant calendar days.

Overall structure by phase

Flow‑Day Modifications (always apply on menstrual days 1–3)
- No high-intensity, no heavy Valsalva, no jumping.
- Replace heavy lifts with:

  - Power: use sled pushes, KB swings, med-ball throws, or pool‑based power alternatives (no vertical jumps)
  - Cardio: low-intensity steady-state (20–35 min walk or easy bike)
- Recovery priorities: increase rest, use heat packs for cramps, diaphragmatic breathing and pelvic floor cues, electrolytes & hydration, gentle stretching/mobility.
- If cramps dizziness or severe symptoms occur, cancel resistance and do rest/active recovery only.

Autoregulation & safety rules
- Use RPE and movement quality. If she reports high fatigue or poor movement following flow, reduce load by 5–10% or shift heavy sets to 3–5 x 6–8 at 60–70% instead of top-end singles/doubles.
- On heavy days, ensure proper warm-up progression, spotters, and rack pins. Use belt only on non-flow heavy sessions if she’s practiced with it.
- If testing, avoid testing on flow days; if flow occurs unexpectedly, postpone or use submax proxy tests.
- Track symptoms and adjust scheduling: keep a log of cycle symptoms, training readiness, and performance. If performance is consistently better in the week after flow, front-load heavier work in that window next cycle where possible.
